body:
N-34 DESIGN, part 3: the repair of the ~650 kept files (slice 5) = refile.py, the machinery N-26 slice 5 will reuse.
WHY NOW: Keeper.handle returns at once when the ref already has a file with a music-server id (_linked, keeper.py:119,124-127), so no re-import fixes them; the bucket is the music server's album list drawn from TAGS. N-26 deferred its slice 5 (test data); this one is the owner's own daily server, so the machinery is built here and N-26's artist rewrite plugs into it later.
SCOPE: only song_file.source='youtube' under Encore/ whose ref has a real album and whose album folder is not the planned one. The Host's own files are never retagged or moved. refile also refuses a ref whose name does not fold whole (P2-25), whoever calls it.
TRIGGER (all true before the first move): (a) slice 4 proof passed on Navidrome 0.64.2; (b) the dry-run report read by the lead (every song rejected only by the tolerance, every non-album type, every multi-candidate song, every held pair; no wrong album); (c) the B-110 reuse fix merged; (d) Database.backup('before-refile') taken, path in the homelab log with the undo; (e) the emulator check of the phone; (f) P2-25 landed (it recomputes norm_key and detaches files of refs the empty key merged).
HOW: an errand of the library link, not a work item. LibraryLinker.run_once runs the errands THEN link_library in one thread (scanner.py:176-190), so the scan cannot meet a moved file before it is linked. work_item.kind is a CHECK list (0002_work.sql:6) and fair-sharing is per person.
PER FILE (journal row first: planned / written / swapped / removed / failed / undone): (1) copy to <album folder>/.name.part, write tags + album picture into the COPY (no tags = no move), os.replace; old file untouched. (2) per batch of 25: ONE start_scan, wait, find_song(..., size=new size) (the music server's own path is built from tags, navidrome.py:144). (3) one transaction: refs.move_file updates the SAME song_file row (path, id, meta; id/added_at/source stay: attach_file would INSERT a second row, refs.py:554-560, and refmerge picks its survivor by added_at) + touch_file + touch_ref_holders. (4) the old file is deleted one pass LATER: until then the music server lists both, and link_library would describe the old id from old tags and attach it as the PREFERRED file (refs.py:554-555), so the scan skips ids the journal says are retiring (refile.retiring_ids) and matches a placed-but-unlinked file by size + title. (5) after deletion a scan; row 'removed'.
NOT PROVEN: whether a retag in place or a move keeps the music-server id, and what getAlbumList2 does: slice 4 is the gate; the design never assumes the id (it reads whatever find_song says).
PHONE (read in the app): the ref id never changes and fileId is a column (encore_writer.dart _companion), so likes, entries, history and downloads stay. COST PROVED: refAudioKey includes the file SIZE (fingerprint.dart:101), a retag changes it, markStaleDownloads + the planner refresh the copy (library_writer.dart:259-279, download_planner.dart:112-126): a downloaded and repaired song is fetched again ONCE on Wi-Fi. The fingerprint comment says tag edits keep the key stable: not true with a size in it. Albums: tombstoned when unseen with a guard (ratio 0.5, from 10 albums, sync_engine.dart:541-566); a matched song replaces one bucket with one real album, so the count does not fall; named test.
OTHER: a playing song (playback_state.playing + ref) is skipped; 100 files / 5 minutes per pass; the lookups are paced by the gate; resumable from the journal; the keeper's free-space floor applies; undo = put back the refs' columns from the DB copy and run the same errand; the audio is never rewritten (only tags). refile_log.ref must be taught to refmerge.FOREIGN_KEY_COLUMNS and the janitor POINTERS. ENCORE_REFILE=0 switches it off.
